questions.question: What happens to your braking distance when you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph?
questions.explanation: When you drive faster, your vehicle has more force and needs more distance to stop. Doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph multiplies your braking distance by four.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the vehicle in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What is the smallest size a placard can be?
questions.explanation: Hazardous material placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches in size.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks collect water and compressor oil that must be drained to prevent damage. You should drain the tanks manually at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle more visible at dawn or dusk?
questions.explanation: At dawn or dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle more easily.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: When using speed to decide when to shift gears, what should you do?

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as your guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: There are two ways to know when to shift: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Read your vehicle's manual to learn the right rpm range for each gear. Then watch your speedometer and learn which speeds each gear handles best. Shift up when needed.

questions.question: When uncoupling a dolly, what should you do?

options.text: Unlock the pintle hook before moving the dolly out from under the rear trailer.
Move the dolly out from under the rear trailer before unlocking the pintle hook.
Remove the dolly as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move the dolly out from under the rear trailer before unlocking the pintle hook.
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is under the rear trailer. The dolly tow bar could fly up and cause serious injury.

questions.question: What should a driver always do?

options.text: Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: While driving, look ahead to spot hazards early. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best way to back up?

options.text: Only use the passenger side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger side whenever possible.

questions.explanation: When backing up, go slowly and use the mirrors on both sides of your vehicle. If you can, use a helper to watch your blind spots. Agree on a signal that means "stop."

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are not leaking

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not leaking
questions.explanation: When inspecting an exhaust system, check that all parts are not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be properly mounted and should not rub against other vehicle parts.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle, the air leakage rate must not be higher than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line. It carries air to the trailer brakes and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: During a brake inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake every time you park a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: How do fully-loaded rigs compare to empty rigs when it comes to rollover risk?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over
They are more likely to roll over
They are equally likely to roll over

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: How long do you have to place emergency warning devices after stopping on the roadside?
questions.explanation: You must place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the roadside. Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when pulling off the road.

questions.question: What should you do when checking your mirrors?

options.text: Do not use the passenger side mirror
Do not use the driver's side mirror
Look in each mirror for long periods of time

questions.explanation: To drive safely, you need to know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Check both mirrors frequently while driving.

questions.question: If you are in a crash, which is NOT a basic procedure you should follow?
questions.explanation: After a crash, you must protect the area, notify the proper authorities, and care for anyone injured. Protecting the accident site helps prevent another crash at the same location.

questions.question: Which type of vehicle is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
